title: Bekhorot 44
description: More blemishes that disqualify a priest from the Temple service: eyes set out of place and Rava’s four words for eye blemishes, Moses’s height, ears, horns and hooves, the swollen belly and why one must never hold back from urinating, and four readings of mero’aḥ ashekh.
topics: 👁️ Eyes set high, low or one of each, and seeing the room and the upper story at once
📖 Rava: why the Torah needs “man,” “blind,” “cataract,” “tevallul” and “in his eye”
📏 Rav: Moses was ten cubits tall, by the cubit of the Tabernacle boards
🐐 The tzime’aḥ, an Arab’s long-eared goat, and horns and hooves removed with their bone
🚻 Torah scholars may urinate in public but not drink in public: Shmuel, his father, and Mar bar Rav Ashi
🙏 “No barren male or female among you”: Reish Lakish and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
🔤 Mero’aḥ ashekh four ways, and Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus’s letter swap

a1.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ כּוֹחֵל שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו כְּאַחַת.

a2.he: שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו לְמַטָּה. מָה ״שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו לְמַעְלָה״ ״שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו לְמַטָּה״? אִילֵּימָא שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו לְמַעְלָה — דְּחָזֵי לְמַעְלָה, שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו לְמַטָּה — דְּחָזֵי לְמַטָּה, עֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְעֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַטָּה — דַּחֲזַאי עֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַטָּה וְעֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה, הַיְינוּ ״רוֹאֶה אֶת הַחֶדֶר וְאֶת הָעֲלִיָּיה כְּאֶחָת״!

a3.he: אֶלָּא, שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו לְמַעְלָה — דְּקָיְימָן לְמַעְלָה, שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו לְמַטָּה — דְּקָיְימָן לְמַטָּה, עֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְעֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַטָּה — דְּקָיְימִי עֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְעֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַטָּה, וְקָיְימִי כְּסִדְרָן נָמֵי, וְרוֹאֶה אֶת הַחֶדֶר וְאֶת הָעֲלִיָּיה כְּאַחַת.

a4.he: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּעֵינוֹ — כׇּל מָה שֶׁבְּעֵינוֹ, מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו לְמַטָּה, שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו לְמַעְלָה, עֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה וְעֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַטָּה, וְרוֹאֶה אֶת הַחֶדֶר וְאֶת הָעֲלִיָּיה כְּאֶחָת, אוֹ שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר עִם חֲבֵירוֹ וְאַחֵר אוֹמֵר: לִי רוֹאֶה.

a5.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עִוֵּר — בֵּין סוֹמֵא בִּשְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו, בֵּין סוֹמֵא בְּאַחַת מֵעֵינָיו. חֲוַרְוָור וְהַמַּיִם הַקְּבוּעִין מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אִישׁ עִוֵּר״.

a6.he: אָמַר רָבָא: לְמָה לִי דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״אִישׁ״, ״עִוֵּר״, ״דַּק״, ״תְּבַלּוּל״, ״בְּעֵינוֹ״? צְרִיכִי, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״עִוֵּר״ מִשּׁוּם דְּלֵיתַנְהוּ כְּלָל, אֲבָל חֲוַרְוָור וְהַמַּיִם הַקְּבוּעִין דְּאִיתַנְהוּ בֵּיהּ — לָא, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״אִישׁ״.

a7.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״אִישׁ״ — מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא קָא חָזֵי כְּלָל, אֲבָל מַחְסוֹרַיְיתָא — לָא, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״דַּק״. וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״דַּק״ — מִשּׁוּם דִּמְחַסְּרָן, אֲבָל מְבַלְבְּלִיתָא — לָא, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״תְּבַלּוּל״.

a8.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״תְּבַלּוּל״ — מִשּׁוּם דִּמְבַלְבְּלָן, אֲבָל מִשּׁוּם מְשַׁנְּיוּתָא — לָא, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״בְּעֵינוֹ״.

a9.he: אָמַר רָבָא: הִלְכָּךְ, כֹּל מֵחֲמַת כַּהְיוּתָא — אָתְיָא מֵ״אִישׁ״, מַחְסוֹרַיְיתָא — מִ״דַּק״, מְבַלְבְּלִיתָא — מִ״תְּבַלּוּל״, מְשַׁנְּיוּתָא — מִ״בְּעֵינוֹ״.

a10.he: סָכֵי שֶׁמֶשׁ. תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: ״סָנֵי שֶׁמֶשׁ״. זַגְדְּיָין. מַחְוֵי רַב הוּנָא: חַד מִדִּידַן וְחַד מִדִּידְהוּ, וְאִיקְּפַד רַב יְהוּדָה.

a11.he: מֵיתִיבִי: שָׁכְבָנָא — שֶׁגְּבִינָיו שׁוֹכְבִים, זַגְדּוֹם — אֶחָד שָׁחוֹר וְאֶחָד לָבָן. תַּנָּא: כֹּל זוּגָא דְּלָא שָׁוֵי לַהֲדָדֵי, ״זַגְדּוֹם״ קָרֵי לֵיהּ.

a12.he: הַצַּיְרָן. עֵינָיו תְּרוּטוֹת, וְצִירָנִיּוֹת, דּוֹמְעוֹת, דּוֹלְפוֹת, טוֹרְדוֹת.

a13.he: תַּנָּא: הַזִּדֵּיר וְהַלּוּפְיָן (וְהַתָּמִיר) [וְהַתִּימְיָן]. זִוֵּיר — דִּמְזַוַּר עֵינֵיהּ, לוּפְיָן — דִּנְפִישִׁין זִיפֵיהּ, (תָּמִיר) [תִּימְיָן] — שֶׁתַּמּוּ (זִיפִין) [זִיפָיו]. וְהָנֵי גַּבֵּי מוּמִין תָּנוּ לְהוּ? וְהָתְנַן: שֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ רִיסֵי עֵינָיו פָּסוּל מִפְּנֵי מַרְאִית הָעַיִן! לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאִשְׁתְּיוּר גַּרְדּוּמֵי, הָא דְּלָא אִישְׁתְּיוּר גַּרְדּוּמֵי.

a14.he: מַתְנִי׳ עֵינָיו גְּדוֹלוֹת כְּשֶׁל עֵגֶל, אוֹ קְטַנּוֹת כְּשֶׁל אַוָּוז. גּוּפוֹ גָּדוֹל מֵאֵבָרָיו, אוֹ קָטָן מֵאֵבָרָיו. חוֹטְמוֹ גָּדוֹל מֵאֵבָרָיו, אוֹ קָטָן מֵאֵיבָרָיו. הַצִומֵּם וְהַצִּומֵּעַ — אֵיזֶהוּ צִומֵּעַ? כֹּל שֶׁאׇזְנָיו קְטַנּוֹת, וְהַצִּומֵּם — כֹּל שֶׁאׇזְנָיו דּוֹמוֹת לִסְפוֹג. שְׂפָתוֹ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה עוֹדֶפֶת עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה עוֹדֶפֶת עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם. וְשֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ שִׁינָּיו — פָּסוּל מִפְּנֵי מַרְאִית הָעַיִן.

a15.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב: מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת הָיָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּפְרֹשׂ אֶת הָאֹהֶל עַל הַמִּשְׁכָּן״, מִי פְּרָשׂוֹ? מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ פְּרָשׂוֹ, וּכְתִיב: ״עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת אוֹרֶךְ הַקָּרֶשׁ״.

a16.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא לְרַב: אִם כֵּן עֲשִׂיתוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ בַּעַל מוּם! דִּתְנַן: גּוּפוֹ גָּדוֹל מֵאֵבָרָיו אוֹ קָטָן מֵאֵבָרָיו. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שִׁימִי! בְּאַמָּה שֶׁל קֹדֶשׁ קָאָמֵינָא.

a17.he: חוֹטְמוֹ גָּדוֹל וכו׳. תָּנָא: כְּאֶצְבַּע קְטַנָּה.

a18.he: הַצִּומֵּם וְהַצִּומֵּעַ. תָּנָא: אַף הַצִּימֵּחַ. לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעִי רַבָּנַן מַאי ״צִימֵּחַ״, שְׁמַעוּ לְהָהוּא טַיָּיעָא דַּהֲוָה קָאָמַר: ״מַאן דְּבָעֵי צִימֵּחַ״, וְאִישְׁתְּכַח גַּדְיָא חֲזִיזָא.

a19.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: עֵז שֶׁאֵין לָהּ קַרְנַיִם, וְרָחֵל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ קַרְנַיִם — כְּשֵׁרִים לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ.

a20.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: יֵשׁ דְּבָרִים שֶׁהֵן כְּמוּמִין, וְאֵינָן כְּמוּמִין, וְשׁוֹחֲטִין עֲלֵיהֶם בְּמִקְדָּשׁ, אֲבָל לֹא בַּמְּדִינָה. וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: עֵז שֶׁאֵין (לוֹ) [לָהּ] קַרְנַיִם, וְרָחֵל שֶׁיֵּשׁ (לוֹ) [לָהּ] קַרְנַיִם, וְהַצִּימֵּחַ, וְהַצִּימֵּם, וְהַצִּימֵּעַ.

a21.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: נִטְּלוּ קַרְנוֹתָן וְזַכְרוּתָן עִמָּהֶן — פְּסוּלָה, וְאֵין פּוֹדִין עֲלֵיהֶם. נִטְּלוּ טְלָפַיִים וְזַכְרוּתָם עִמָּהֶן — פְּסוּלִין, וְנִפְדִּין עֲלֵיהֶם.

a22.he: מֵיתִיבִי: נִטְּלוּ קַרְנַיִין וּטְלָפַיִין וְזַכְרוּתָן עִמָּהֶן — פְּסוּלִין וְנִפְדִּין עֲלֵיהֶן! לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּאִיתְעֲקוּר אִיתְעֲקוֹרֵי, הָא דְּאִיגּוּם אִיגּוֹמֵי.

a23.he: וּדְאִיגּוּם אִיגּוֹמֵי, פָּסוּל? וּרְמִינְהוּ: פָּרָה שֶׁקַּרְנֶיהָ וּטְלָפֶיהָ שְׁחוֹרִים — יָגוֹד! תַּרְגְּמַהּ זְעֵירִי: מֵעִילָּוֵי זַכְרוּת.

b1.he: מַתְנִי׳ דַּדִּין שׁוֹכְבִין כְּשֶׁל אִשָּׁה, כְּרֵיסוֹ צָבָה, טִיבּוּרוֹ יוֹצֵא, נִכְפֶּה — אֲפִילּוּ אַחַת לְיָמִים, רוּחַ קְצָרָה בָּאָה עָלָיו, הַמְאוּשְׁבָּן, וּבַעַל גֶּבֶר.

b2.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: מַשְׁתִּינִין מַיִם בִּפְנֵי רַבִּים, וְאֵין שׁוֹתִין מַיִם בִּפְנֵי רַבִּים. וְתַנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: מַשְׁתִּינִין מַיִם בִּפְנֵי רַבִּים, וְאֵין שׁוֹתִין מַיִם בִּפְנֵי רַבִּים. וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ לְהַשְׁתִּין מַיִם וְלֹא הִשְׁתִּין, וְנִמְצָא כְּרֵיסוֹ צָבָה.

b3.he: שְׁמוּאֵל אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ בְּשַׁבְּתָא דְרִגְלָא, נְגַדוּ לֵיהּ גְּלִימָא, אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דַּאֲבוּהּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֶתֵּן לָךְ אַרְבַּע מְאָה זוּזֵי וְזִיל אַהְדַּר עוֹבָדָא. אַתְּ — דְּאֶפְשָׁר לָךְ, דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר לֵיהּ — לִיסְתַּכַּן.

b4.he: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אִיצְטְרִיךְ אַגּוּדָּא גַּמְלָא, אַשְׁתֵּין. אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: חֲמָתָךְ קָאָתְיָא! אֲמַר לְהוּ: בְּאוּדְנַהּ.

b6.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁנֵי נְקָבִים יֵשׁ בּוֹ בָּאָדָם, אֶחָד מוֹצִיא שֶׁתֶן וְאֶחָד מוֹצִיא שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע, וְאֵין בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה אֶלָּא כִּקְלִיפַּת הַשּׁוּם. בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָדָם נִצְרָךְ, אִם נִקְּבוּ זֶה לְתוֹךְ זֶה — נִמְצָא עָקָר.

b7.he: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״לֹא יִהְיֶה בְךָ עָקָר וַעֲקָרָה וּבִבְהֶמְתֶּךָ״? אֵימָתַי לֹא יִהְיֶה בְךָ עָקָר? בִּזְמַן שֶׁ״בִּבְהֶמְתֶּךָ״.

b8.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: ״לֹא יִהְיֶה בְךָ עָקָר״ — מִן הַתַּלְמִידִים, ״וַעֲקָרָה״ — שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא תְּפִלָּתֶךָ עֲקוּרָה לִפְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם. אֵימָתַי? בִּזְמַן שֶׁאַתָּה מֵשִׂים עַצְמְךָ כִּבְהֵמָה.

b9.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לֹא יַשְׁתִּין אָדָם מַיִם לֹא עַל כְּלֵי חֶרֶס, וְלֹא עַל מְקוֹם קָשֶׁה, דְּאָמַר רַב: הָנֵי מְדוֹרֵי דְּבָבֶל מְהַדְּרִי מַיָּא לְעֵין עֵיטָם. אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָא אִיתְּתָא לָא תְּקוּם לְהֶדְיָא בְּאַנְפֵּי יָנוֹקָא, אַגִּיסָא לֵית לַן בַּהּ.

b10.he: תַּנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: עַמּוּד הַחוֹזֵר מֵבִיא אָדָם לִידֵי הִדְרוֹקָן, סִילוֹן הַחוֹזֵר מֵבִיא אָדָם לִידֵי יֵרָקוֹן. אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא, אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: דָּם רָבֶה — שְׁחִין רָבֶה, שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע רָבָה — צָרַעַת רָבָה, צוֹאָה רָבָה — הִדְרוֹקָן רָבֶה, מֵי רַגְלַיִם רָבִין — יֵרָקוֹן רָבֶה.

b11.he: רוּחַ קַצְרִית בָּאָה עָלָיו. מַאי נִינְהוּ? תָּנָא: רוּחַ בֶּן נְפָלִים בָּאָה עָלָיו.

b12.he: הַמְאוּשְׁבָּן וּבַעַל גֶּבֶר. תָּנָא: מְשׁוּבָּן בַּבֵּיצִים, וּבַעַל גֶּבֶר בַּגִּיד. תָּנָא: מְשׁוּבָּן — זֶה הַקַּיָּין, הַגְרַבְתָּן — זֶה בַּעַל קִיק; קַיָּין — בַּבֵּיצִים, גְּרַבְתָּא — בַּגִּיד.

b13.he: וְעַד כַּמָּה? מַחְוֵי רַב יְהוּדָה: עַד רְכוּבָּה. תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: עַד רְכוּבָּה — פָּסוּל, לְמַעְלָה מִן רְכוּבָּה — כָּשֵׁר. אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: עַד רְכוּבָּה — כָּשֵׁר, לְמַטָּה מִן הָרְכוּבָּה — פָּסוּל.

b14.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין לוֹ בֵּיצִים, אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת — הֲרֵי זֶה ״מְרוֹחַ אָשֶׁךְ״ הָאָמוּר בְּתוֹרָה. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁנִּימּוֹחוּ אֲשָׁכָיו. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁרוּחַ בַּאֲשָׁכָיו. רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁמַּרְאָיו חֲשׁוּכִין.

b15.he: גְּמָ׳ קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: הָא ״חֲסַר אָשֶׁךְ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! תְּנִי: שֶׁנִּמְרְחוּ אֲשָׁכָיו. קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: הַאי ״מַמְרוֹחַ אָשֶׁךְ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! תְּנִי: שֶׁהָרוּחַ בַּאֲשָׁכָיו.

b16.he: קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס: הַאי ״רוּחַ אָשֶׁךְ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! תְּנִי שֶׁמַּרְאָיו חֲשׁוּכִין, קָסָבַר גּוֹרְעִין וּמוֹסִיפִין וְדוֹרְשִׁין.

b17.he: הַיְינוּ כּוּשִׁי! רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס לָא תָּנֵי ״כּוּשִׁי״.

messages.text: Continued from 43b: a baraita defined the ḥarum as a priest whose nose is sunk. Rabbi Yosei said a ḥarum is only one who can paint both his eyes in a single stroke, and the Sages said to him: You have gone too far.
@Rabbi Yosei Rather, even if he does not paint both of his eyes as one, any priest with an abnormally sunken nose is considered a ḥarum.

The mishna teaches that if both of one’s eyes are above or both of his eyes are below, he is disqualified from performing the Temple service. What does the mishna mean when it mentions a priest wherein both of his eyes are above or both of his eyes are below?

If we say that the phrase: Both of his eyes are above, means that he constantly gazes upward, and the phrase: Both of his eyes are below, means that he constantly gazes downward, then the case where one of his eyes is above and one of his eyes is below must similarly mean that he gazes with one of his eyes downward and one of his eyes upward. But if so, this is identical to the next case in the mishna, that one sees both the room on the ground floor and the upper story as one.

notes.he:
שעומדות במקומן בסדר אבל כל שעה רואות למעלה:
חדר למטה עלייה למעלה:
notes.en: That he gazes upward: [his eyes] stand in their place in proper order, but they look upward all the time. The ḥeder [room] is below; the aliyya [upper story] is above.

messages.text: Rather, the phrase: Both of his eyes are above, is referring to a case where his eyes are situated above their normal place, and the phrase: Both of his eyes are below, is referring to a case where his eyes are situated below their normal place. Similarly, the case where one of his eyes is above and one of his eyes is below is where one of his eyes is situated above and one of his eyes is situated below.

notes.he: בגובה המצח שלא כשאר בני אדם:
notes.en: That are situated above: at the height of the forehead, not as with other people.

messages.text: And the mishna adds that in a case where his eyes are situated in their proper arrangement as well, but he sees the room on the ground floor and the upper story as one, he too is considered blemished.

notes.he: כלומר והינן עומדות במקומן כסדר אבל רואה את החדר ואת העליה שעינו אחת רואה למעלה ועינו אחת רואה למטה:
notes.en: And they are situated in their order: that is, they stand in their place in order, but he sees the room and the upper story, for one eye sees upward and one eye sees downward.

messages.text: From where are these matters derived? As the Sages taught in a baraita:

The verse states with regard to blemishes that disqualify priests: “Or a cataract or a tevallul in his eye.” Since it is obvious that a cataract or a tevallul can occur only in one’s eyes, why does the verse state: In his eye? The term “in his eye” indicates that any blemish that is in his eye disqualifies him from performing the Temple service.

verse.he: אוֹ־גִבֵּן אוֹ־דַק אוֹ תְּבַלֻּל בְּעֵינוֹ אוֹ גָרָב אוֹ יַלֶּפֶת אוֹ מְרוֹחַ אָשֶׁךְ׃
verse.en: or who is a hunchback, or a dwarf, or who has a growth in his eye, or who has a boil-scar, or scurvy, or crushed testes.

notes.he: תבלול בעינו דהוה ליה למכתב דק תבלול ואנא ידענא דלא שייכא אלא בעין:
notes.en: In his eye: “tevallul in his eye.” It could have written just “dak, tevallul,” and I would know that this applies only to the eye.

notes.he: דכתיב או תבלול בעינו:
notes.en: In his eye: as it is written, “or tevallul in his eye.”

messages.text: From here the Sages stated: If both of his eyes are below or both of his eyes are above, or if one of his eyes is above and one of his eyes is below, or if he sees the room and the upper story as one, or if when he speaks with his friend another person says: He is looking at me, he is blemished and is disqualified from performing the Temple service.

When it is stated that a blind man [iver] is disqualified from performing the Temple service, this applies whether he is blind in both of his eyes or blind in one of his eyes. With regard to a priest who cannot see due to pale spots on the eye or due to tears streaming from the eye that are constant, from where is it derived that he is disqualified? The same verse states: “A blind man [ish iver].” The superfluous word “ish” serves to include these conditions as well.

verse.he: כִּי כׇל־אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ מוּם לֹא יִקְרָב אִישׁ עִוֵּר אוֹ פִסֵּחַ אוֹ חָרֻם אוֹ שָׂרוּעַ׃
verse.en: No one at all who has a defect shall be qualified: no man who is blind, or lame, or has a limb too short or too long;

notes.he: מריבויא דאיש:
notes.en: A blind man [ish iver]: from the inclusion of the word ish [man].

messages.text: Why do I need the Merciful One to write the terms “man,” “blind,” “cataract,” “tevallul,” and “in his eye” (Leviticus 21:18, 20)?

All these are necessary, as had the Merciful One written only “blind,” then one might say that a blind person is disqualified because his eyes are not in their sockets at all, i.e., they were enucleated. But in the case of a priest with pale spots on the eye or tears streaming from the eye that are constant, where his eyes are still in their sockets but he cannot see, perhaps he is not considered blemished. Therefore, the Merciful One wrote “man” to include these conditions as well.

notes.he: משמע שניטלו עיניו וליתנהו כלל:
notes.en: Blind [iver]: implies that his eyes were taken away and are not there at all.

notes.he: לעיניה:
notes.en: That are not there at all: his eyes.

messages.text: And had the Merciful One written only “man,” one might have thought that only total blindness disqualifies a priest, because he cannot see at all. But if his condition causes merely impaired vision, then he is not considered blemished. Therefore, the Merciful One wrote “cataract” to include conditions of impaired vision as well.

notes.he: שחסרה מראיתו אבל רואה מקצת:
notes.en: Impairment [maḥsoraita]: his sight is diminished, but he sees somewhat.

notes.he: טייל"א מחסרת המראה ואינו ניטל:
notes.en: Dak [cataract]: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss.) It diminishes the sight but does not take it away.

messages.text: And had the Merciful One written only that a priest with a cataract is disqualified, it might have been thought that such a priest is disqualified because his vision is impaired. But if his vision is not impaired but his eyes are mixed, i.e., the black and white parts of his eyes are mixed together, then he is not disqualified. Therefore, the Merciful One wrote “tevallul.”

notes.he: לבן הפוסק בסירה ונכנס בשחור ואינו מקצר המראית כלל:
notes.en: Intermingling [mevalbelita]: the white breaks across the rim and enters the black, and it does not shorten the sight at all.

notes.he: שנפחת קצת ממראות עיניו כתב רחמנא דק והיינו מחסוריתא אבל מבלבליתא לא. שמבולבל לבן בשחור:
notes.en: But impairment [maḥsoraita]: where the sight of his eyes is somewhat diminished, the Merciful One wrote dak, and that is maḥsoraita; but intermingling [mevalbelita], no: where the white is mixed into the black.

messages.text: And had the Merciful One written only “tevallul,” one might say that this disqualifies a priest because his eyes are mixed. But the Torah does not disqualify a priest due to a deviation from normal appearance, e.g., especially large eyes, or eyes situated higher than normal. Therefore, the Merciful One wrote “in his eye.”

notes.he: שמשונות במעמדן כגון למעלה או למטה או רואה חדר ועלייה כאחת:
notes.en: Deviations [meshanyuta]: eyes that are unusual in their position, such as above or below, or seeing the room and the upper story at once.

notes.he: שמשונה מראה עיניו:
notes.en: But deviations: where the look of his eyes is unusual.

messages.text: Therefore, all blemishes of the eyes that disqualify a priest on account of dimness, i.e., blindness, are derived from the term “man.” All blemishes of the eyes that are related to vision impairment are derived from “cataract.” All blemishes that are related to parts of the eye being intermingled are derived from “tevallul.” Finally, the disqualification of deviations is derived from “in his eye.”

notes.he: דאינו רואה:
notes.en: Dimness [kahyuta]: that he does not see.

notes.he: דהני חורוור והמים הקבועין כהיותא נינהו ומפיק להו תנא דברייתא מאיש:
notes.en: Is derived from “man”: for these pale spots and constant tears are a kind of dimness, and the tanna of the baraita derives them from “man.”

notes.he: שאינו רואה כלל:
notes.en: Dimness [kahyuta]: that he does not see at all.

messages.caption: Rava: five words in the verses, each covering another kind of eye blemish.

messages.text: The mishna teaches that those unable to look at the sun [sakhei shemesh] are disqualified from performing the Temple service.
Those who hate the sun [sanei shemesh], i.e., they are incapable of opening their eyes in sunlight.
messages.lead: Rav Yosef taught that this is a reference to:

notes.dh: סכי שמש תני רב יוסף סני שמש
notes.he: ששונא את השמש ואינו יכול לראות מקום שחמה זורחת שם:
notes.en: Sakhei shemesh: Rav Yosef taught “sanei shemesh”: one who hates the sun and cannot look at a place where the sun is shining.

notes.he: תני רב יוסף היינו סני שמש שאינו יכול להסתכל בשמשו:
notes.en: Sakhei shemesh: Rav Yosef taught that this is sanei shemesh, one who cannot look at the sunlight.

messages.text: The mishna further states that one whose eyes are different is disqualified from performing the Temple service.
The term: Different eyes, is referring to an individual wherein one of his eyes is like ours and one of his eyes is like theirs.
messages.lead: In order to illustrate this blemish, Rav Huna pointed with his finger while saying:

notes.he: שיש לו עין אחת דומה לעין אלו היושבין נגדי ועין אחת שלי. רב יהודה היה יושב כנגדו והיו עיניו משונות:
notes.en: One of ours and one of theirs: he has one eye like the eye of these who sit opposite me, and one eye like mine. Rav Yehuda was sitting opposite him, and his eyes were unusual.

notes.he: פירוש רב יהודה שהיה לפניו פי' בקונט' שהיו עיניו משונות ולא פירש במה היו משונות ור"ת מפרש דרב יהודה אריך בדורו הוה דאמר בפרק המפלת (נדה דף כד:) ורב הונא איניש גוצא הוה כדאי' במסכת תעניות פרקא דחסידים ומשום הכי לא היו עיניו נכרות קטנות כ"כ משל סתם בני אדם אבל משל רב יהודה היו נכרות שהיו גדולות הרבה ולכך הקפיד רב יהודה והיינו שינוי דעינו אחת גדולה ואחת קטנה ואע"ג דלא הוי מומא לענין אחולי עבודה עד שתהא גדולה כשל עגל או קטנה כשל אווז מכל מקום אין זה שוה בזרעו של אהרן:
notes.en: Rav Huna pointed: one of theirs: that is, of Rav Yehuda, who was before him. Rashi explained that his eyes were unusual, but did not explain how they were unusual. Rabbeinu Tam explains: Rav Yehuda was the tallest man of his generation, as it says in chapter HaMapelet (Nidda 24b), and Rav Huna was a short man, as is stated in tractate Ta’anit, in the chapter about the pious. Therefore [Rav Huna’s] eyes did not look noticeably smaller than those of ordinary people, but next to Rav Yehuda’s they did, for his were very large. That is why Rav Yehuda took offense. And this is the “difference”: one eye large and one small. And even though this is not a blemish that would profane the service unless the eye is as large as a calf’s or as small as a goose’s, nonetheless such a one is not like the rest of the offspring of Aaron.

notes.dh: זגדים מחוי רב הונא חדא מדידן וחדא מדידהו
notes.he: היינו שעינו אחת בריאה דומה לשלנו והאחרת דומה לאותן שעיניהם משונות:
notes.en: Zagdim: Rav Huna pointed: one of ours and one of theirs. That is, one of his eyes is healthy, like ours, and the other is like those of people whose eyes are unusual.

messages.text: And since Rav Huna was pointing at Rav Yehuda, who had abnormal eyes, Rav Yehuda took offense.

notes.he: מפני שהוא היה כן. וגרם שכביא הצירי:
notes.en: And Rav Yehuda took offense: because he was like that. [The note ends with a few words, “vegeres shekhavya hatzeiri,” which seem to give Rabbeinu Gershom’s reading of the next lemmas, shekhavna and hatzayran; the printed text is unclear.]

messages.text: When the Sages taught that a shekhavna is disqualified from performing the Temple service, they were referring to one whose eyebrows lie flat [shokhvim] and cover his eyes. When they taught that one whose eyes are different [zagdum] is disqualified, they were referring to a case where one of his eyebrows is black and one is white.
messages.lead: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita to Rav Huna’s interpretation of one whose eyes are different:
messages.quote: one of his eyes is like ours and one of his eyes is like theirs

notes.he: שגביניו ארוכין ושוכבין על עיניו:
notes.en: Shekhavna: whose eyebrows are long and lie over his eyes.

messages.text: With regard to any pair of limbs that are not identical to one another, the tanna of this baraita calls them different.
The mishna teaches that one whose eyes tear constantly is disqualified from performing the Temple service. The Gemara cites a baraita that defines such an individual:
His eyes, i.e., his eyelids, droop and can open only partially, or his eyes are round; his eyes tear, or tears stream from his eyes, or tears flow intensely from them.

notes.he: עגולות:
notes.en: Terutot: round.

notes.he: עגולות יותר מתרוטות:
notes.en: And tziraniyyot: rounder than terutot.

notes.he: מעט:
notes.en: Tearing [dome’ot]: a little.

notes.he: יותר מדומעות:
notes.en: Streaming [dolfot]: more than tearing.

notes.he: יותר מדולפות כמו (משלי כז) דלף טורד:
notes.en: Flowing [toredot]: more than streaming, as in “a continual dripping [delef tored]” (Proverbs 27:15).

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס עגולות כמו כי תרוטה בסנהדרין (דף קז) גבי לבנה וצירניות פירש בקונט' עגולות יותר מתרוטות ותימה כיון דתנא קילתא כ"ש חמירתא וכענין זה קשה גבי דתנא דומעות דולפות וטורדות דולפות יותר מדומעות וטורדות יותר מדולפות ושמא איצטריך למיתני כולהו לאשמועינן דלא מיפסלי משום מומא אלא משום דאין שוה בזרעו של אהרן:
notes.en: His eyes are terutot: Rashi explained “round,” as in “for it is terutah” in Sanhedrin (107), said of the moon; and tziraniyyot, Rashi explained, rounder than terutot. This is puzzling: once he teaches the lighter case, all the more so the more severe one! The same difficulty arises where he teaches dome’ot, dolfot and toredot, since dolfot is more than dome’ot and toredot is more than dolfot. Perhaps it was necessary to teach them all to tell us that they are disqualified not as a blemish but because such a one is not like the rest of the offspring of Aaron.

notes.he: עגולות:
notes.en: Terutot: round.

notes.he: שעגול אותו מקום שהעין מונח בו:
notes.en: Tziraniyyot: the place where the eye sits is round.

notes.he: יותר מדומעות:
notes.en: Dolfot: more than dome’ot.

notes.he: שדולפות בלא הפסק. ואיכא דאמרי טורדות שאין יכול לעצום עיניו אלא בטורח גדול למ"ה. זיוור דמזוורן עיניה. מטמרין עיניו:
notes.en: Toredot: that drip without stopping. And some say toredot means that he can close his eyes only with great effort. [The note runs on into the next baraita:] Zivver: whose eyes are askew. [A garbled word follows, apparently:] his eyes are hidden.

messages.text: The zadir, and the lupin, and the tamir are disqualified from performing the Temple service. Zadir is a reference to one whose eyes are strange. Lupin is a reference to one with an abundance of eyelashes. Tamir is a reference to one whose eyelashes are depleted.

notes.he: הוי מום דמזורדן עיניו:
notes.en: It is taught: also the zadir, the lupin and the timyan: it is a blemish, for his eyes are askew.

notes.he: דנפיש זיפי שריסי עיניו גדולות:
notes.en: Lupin: whose lashes are many; the hairs of his eyelids are large.

notes.he: דלית ביה ריסי עינים כלל:
notes.en: And the timin, whose lashes are gone: who has no eyelashes at all.

messages.text: And does the tanna teach these cases together with full-fledged blemishes? But didn’t we learn in the mishna: One whose eyelashes have fallen out is disqualified from performing the Temple service due to the appearance of a blemish? Clearly, this is not considered an actual blemish.
messages.quote: Tamir is a reference to one whose eyelashes are depleted

notes.he: להאי תומיין מי הוי מום והא לא פסיל ליה מתני' אלא משום מראית העין:
notes.en: But does he teach these together with blemishes?: is this timyan [one whose lashes are depleted] a blemish? Our mishna disqualifies him only because of the appearance!

messages.text: It is not difficult. This mishna is referring to a case where the roots of his eyelashes remain, whereas that baraita is referring to a case where the roots do not remain.

notes.he: שרשין לא הוי מום אלא משום מראית העין:
notes.en: Where the stumps remained: the roots [remain]; then it is not a blemish, only [a disqualification] because of the appearance.

notes.he: הני דמוסיף תנא ברא הא דאישתייר גרדומי כלומר אע"ג דנשתייר עיקרו פוסל:
notes.en: It is not difficult: those that the outside tanna [of the baraita] adds are where stumps remained; that is, even though the root remained, it disqualifies. [Rabbeinu Gershom pairs the two cases the opposite way from Rashi and the English translation.]

notes.he: דמתניתין דלא אישתיור מגרדומי כלל:
notes.en: And that one, of our mishna: where no stumps remained at all.

messages.text: Mishna
The mishna lists additional blemishes that disqualify a priest from performing the Temple service: If a priest’s eyes are large like those of a calf or small like those of a goose;
if his body is disproportionately large relative to his limbs or disproportionately small relative to his limbs;

notes.he: כגון ידיו ורגליו ושוקיו:
notes.en: Relative to his limbs: such as his arms, his legs and his shins.

messages.text: if his nose is disproportionately large relative to his limbs or disproportionately small relative to his limbs, he is disqualified.
And the tzomem and the tzome’a are also disqualified. What is a tzome’a? It is anyone whose ears are small. And what is the tzomem? It is anyone whose ears are similar to a sponge.

notes.he: במתני' מפרש לה:
notes.en: Tzimem, tzime’a: the mishna explains them.

notes.he: שכווצות וסתומות:
notes.en: Similar to a sponge: shriveled and closed.

messages.text: If his upper lip protrudes beyond the lower lip or his lower lip protrudes beyond the upper lip, that is a blemish.
And one whose teeth fell out is disqualified due to the appearance of a blemish.
Gemara
Moses, our teacher, was ten ammot tall, as it is stated: “And he spread the tent over the Tabernacle.”

verse.he: וַיִּפְרֹשׂ אֶת־הָאֹהֶל עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּן וַיָּשֶׂם אֶת־מִכְסֵה הָאֹהֶל עָלָיו מִלְמָעְלָה כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶת־מֹשֶׁה׃ {ס}
verse.en: He spread the tent over the Tabernacle, placing the covering of the tent on top of it—just as GOD had commanded Moses.

notes.he: קס"ד באמה שלו:
notes.en: Ten ammot: it was assumed [at first] that he meant by Moses’s own cubit.

messages.text: Who spread the tent over the Tabernacle? Moses, our teacher, spread it, and it is written with regard to the height of the Tabernacle: “Ten ammot shall be the length of a board.” Moses must have been at least as tall as the Tabernacle itself for him to have spread the tent over it.

verse.he: עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת אֹרֶךְ הַקָּרֶשׁ וְאַמָּה וַחֲצִי הָאַמָּה רֹחַב הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָאֶחָד׃
verse.en: The length of each plank shall be ten cubits and the width of each plank a cubit and a half.

messages.text: @Rav If so, you have rendered Moses, our teacher, a blemished person, as we learned in the mishna: If one’s body is disproportionately large relative to his limbs or disproportionately small relative to his limbs, then he is blemished. A typical person is no more than three arm-lengths [ammot] tall, and yet Moses was apparently ten times taller than the length of his own arm.
messages.quote: Moses, our teacher, was ten ammot tall

notes.he: דגופו גדול מזרועותיו דהא כל אדם אין גופו אלא שלש אמות באמתו:
notes.en: A blemished person: for his body is larger than his arms, since no person’s body is more than three cubits by his own cubit.

messages.text: Shimi, when I said that Moses was ten ammot tall, I said so in reference to the cubit [amma] of a board used in the building of the Tabernacle. The limbs of Moses were proportional to the rest of his body, but he was indeed ten cubits tall.
messages.quote: you have rendered Moses, our teacher, a blemished person

notes.he: דהיינו עשר אמה באמה של קרשים דאורך הקרשים לא נמדד באמתו של משה. והא דאמרן בפירקא דלעיל (בכורות דף מ.) אחת יתירה על של משה חצי אצבע לאו בשל משה ממש קאמר דודאי של משה היתה יתירה מאד על אותה של קדש שתיקן משה:
notes.en: I was speaking of the cubit of the boards: that is, ten cubits by the cubit of the boards, for the length of the boards was not measured by Moses’s own cubit. And what we said in the previous chapter (Bekhorot 40a), “one longer than that of Moses by half a fingerbreadth,” does not mean Moses’s own cubit literally, for Moses’s own cubit was certainly far longer than the sacred cubit that Moses established.

notes.he: דהוה משה רבנו י' אמות באמותיו שלו לא היה אלא ג' אמות שלו כדרך כל אדם שגבוה ג' אמות שלו:
notes.en: Shimi, I was speaking of the sacred cubit: that Moses our teacher was ten cubits [by that cubit]; by his own cubits he was only three cubits, like every person, who is three of his own cubits tall.

messages.text: The measure of disproportion is the size of one’s small finger.
messages.lead: The mishna taught that if one’s nose is disproportionately large relative to his limbs, he is blemished. The Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: his nose is disproportionately large relative to his limbs

notes.he: אם חוטמו גדול לפי שאר אברין יותר מדאי כשיעור רוחב אצבע קטנה הוי מום היכי משערינן ליה מודדין חוטמו לחוטם בני אדם הארוכין בגופן כמוהו:
notes.en: Like a small finger: if his nose is too large for his other limbs by the measure of the width of a small finger, it is a blemish. How do we gauge it? We measure his nose against the noses of people as tall as he is.

notes.he: הא קטן או גדול הוי מום:
notes.en: It is taught: up to the thickness of a small finger [it is fit]; beyond that, smaller or larger, is a blemish.

messages.text: The tzime’aḥ is also disqualified from performing the Temple service.

notes.he: דומות לספוג מקובצות ביחד:
notes.en: Similar to a sponge: bunched together.

messages.text: The Sages did not know what a tzime’aḥ is. They heard a certain Arab who was saying: Who wants a tzime’aḥ, and it was found to be a long-eared goat.

notes.he: אזניו ארוכות מאד עד שתכופות למטה:
notes.en: Ḥaziza: its ears are very long, so that they bend downward.

notes.he: שאזניו תלויות לו למטה:
notes.en: A gadya ḥaziza: whose ears hang down.

messages.text: A female goat that has no horns and a female lamb that has horns are fit for sacrificing upon the altar, i.e., they are not considered blemished, despite the fact that they differ from regular female goats and female lambs.
messages.lead: The Gemara discusses the halakha of a tzomem, tzome’a, and tzime’aḥ with regard to animals.

messages.text: This is also taught in a baraita:

There are matters that appear like blemishes but they are not truly like blemishes, and one may therefore slaughter sacrificial animals on account of them in the Temple, i.e., they are fit for sacrifice despite these blemishes; but if they are firstborn animals, they are not permitted for slaughter in the rest of the country on account of these blemishes, as the unique physical characteristics of these animals are not true blemishes. And these are the blemishes: A female goat that has no horns, and a female lamb that has horns, and the tzime’aḥ, and the tzomem, and the tzome’a.

notes.he: דלא הוי מום:
notes.en: In the Temple: since it is not a blemish.

notes.he: ומתני' דחשיב להו (באדם מומין) קאמר לפי שאינו שוה בזרעו של אהרן:
notes.en: And the tzime’aḥ, the tzimem and the tzime’a: and our mishna, which counts them [as blemishes in a person], does so because such a one is not like the rest of the offspring of Aaron.

messages.text: If the horns of an animal were removed, and their bones, i.e., the bones inside the horns, were removed with them, the animal is unfit for sacrifice. But even so, one may not redeem the animal on account of such blemishes, as they are not full-fledged blemishes.
messages.lead: With regard to the horns of an animal:

notes.he: היינו עצם התחוב בתוך הקרניים: זכרות הטלפים היינו עצם שבתוך הטלפים דזו היא כף הרגל:
notes.en: Their core [zakhrut]: that is the bone inserted inside the horns. The core of the hooves is the bone inside the hooves, which is the sole of the foot.

notes.he: אם בהמת שאר קדשים שאינה בכור אינה נפדית בכך דלא הוי מום גמור אלא לאיפסולי:
notes.en: And one may not redeem them: if it is an animal of other offerings, not a firstborn, it is not redeemed for this, since it is not a full blemish, only enough to disqualify it.

notes.he: העצם שבפנים פסולה להקרבה:
notes.en: And their core with them: the bone inside; it is disqualified from being offered.

messages.text: But if the hooves were removed, and their bones, i.e., the portion of the leg to which the hooves are attached, were removed with them, they are unfit for sacrifice and they are even redeemed on account of such blemishes, as they are full-fledged blemishes.
If the horns or the hooves of an animal were removed, and their respective bones were removed with them, they are unfit and they are redeemed on account of them.
messages.lead: Rav Ḥisda stated that the removal of a horn and its bone is not considered a full-fledged blemish that enables the animal to be redeemed. The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita:
messages.quote: one may not redeem the animal on account of such blemishes

notes.he: וקשיא לרב חסדא דאמר אין נפדין:
notes.en: And they are redeemed for them: this is difficult for Rav Ḥisda, who said they are not redeemed.

messages.text: It is not difficult. This baraita is referring to a case where the bone was entirely uprooted, which is a full-fledged blemish on account of which the animal may be redeemed. That statement of Rav Ḥisda is referring to a case where the bones were cut but were not uprooted entirely.

notes.he: קרנים ושרשי הזכרות ונראית גומא בראש:
notes.en: The baraita, which teaches it, is where they were uprooted: the horns and the roots of the core, so that a hollow is visible in the head.

notes.he: נחתכין מלמעלה ושרשיו נשארו:
notes.en: Rav Ḥisda, where they were cut: they were cut from above, and their roots remained.

notes.he: דנשתייר מקצת מזכרותן אין נפדית עליהן:
notes.en: This is where they were cut: some of their core remained, so it is not redeemed for them.

messages.text: But in a case where the bones of the animal were cut, is the animal even rendered unfit?

notes.he: מי שייך בה אפילו פסלות:
notes.en: And where they were cut: does even a disqualification apply to it?

messages.text: And the Gemara raises a contradiction from a mishna:
With regard to a red heifer whose horns and hooves are black, the halakha is that one should cut away the black parts so that the heifer remains entirely red.

notes.he: אדומה:
notes.en: Heifer: the red heifer.

notes.he: יחתוך כמו (דניאל ד) גודו אילנא:
notes.en: Yagod: he should cut, as in “Hew down [godu] the tree” (Daniel 4:11).

notes.he: פרה אדומה שקרניה שחורות בראשו יגור במגרה אותו שחור ותהיה כשרה קסבר אף על גב דחתך מזכרותן:
notes.en: A red heifer whose horns are black at the tip: he should saw off that black part with a saw, and it is fit. He holds [this] even though he cut into their core.

messages.text: Evidently, cutting away the horns of the heifer does not inflict a blemish upon it.
It refers to cutting the horn specifically from above the bone inside it. In such a case, the heifer is not disqualified. Cutting the bone itself does disqualify the animal.

notes.he: האי [דקתני] יחתוך מעילווי זכרותייהו שיש בחודו של קרן כשתים ושלש אצבעות שאין זכרות מגיע שם ואם השחרות אין מגיע עד מקום הזכרות יחתוך אבל יותר מכאן פסולה:
notes.en: Ze’eiri interpreted it: what it teaches, “he should cut,” means above their core, for at the tip of the horn there are some two or three fingerbreadths that the core does not reach. If the blackness does not reach the place of the core, he may cut it; but beyond that, it is disqualified.

notes.he: לא תרגמא זעירי מעילוי דכרותיהו חתך ולא איפסלה:
notes.en: No: Ze’eiri interpreted it: he cut above their core, and so it is not disqualified.

messages.text: Mishna
The mishna lists additional blemishes that disqualify a priest from performing the Temple service: One who has breasts so large that they sag like those of a woman;

notes.he: גדולים:
notes.en: Breasts that sag: large.

messages.text: or if one’s belly is swollen and protrudes; or if one’s navel protrudes;
or if one is an epileptic, even if he experiences seizures only once in a long while;

notes.he: נופל מחמת חולי:
notes.en: An epileptic [nikhpe]: one who falls because of illness.

notes.he: שאינו נופל אלא פעם אחת לימים שתבא לזמן קבוע:
notes.en: Once in a while: he falls only once in a while, at a fixed time.

notes.he: כלומר אפילו לזמן קבוע פסול לעבודה אפילו בשאר הימים בשאינו נכפה:
notes.en: An epileptic, even once in a while: that is, even if [he falls only] at a fixed time, he is disqualified for the service even on the other days, when he does not fall.

messages.text: or one who is afflicted with a melancholy temper;

notes.he: רוח שד:
notes.en: A melancholy temper [ruaḥ ketzara]: a demon’s spirit.

messages.text: or one whose scrotum is unnaturally long; or one whose penis is unnaturally long is disqualified from performing the Temple service.

notes.he: ביציו גדולים:
notes.en: Me’ushban: his testicles are large.

notes.he: גידו גדול:
notes.en: Ba’al gever: his member is large.

messages.text: Gemara

Torah scholars may urinate in public and they need not be concerned with issues of modesty, because holding back from urinating causes bodily harm. But they may not drink water in public, as such conduct is unbefitting a Torah scholar.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites a halakha involving a swollen belly.

notes.he: דדרך תלמיד חכם להיות צנוע באכילה ובשתיה אבל להטיל מים לא ליהוי צנוע שמא ימתין ויסתכן:
notes.en: And they may not drink water: for it is the way of a Torah scholar to be modest in eating and drinking; but in urinating he should not be modest, lest he wait and endanger himself.

notes.he: פירש בקונטרס דרך ת"ח להיות צנוע באכילה ושתיה והא דאמר בסוף כיצד צולין (פסחים דף פו:) דרב הונא בריה דרב נתן אשתי כסא בתרי זמני ולא מהדר אפיה וקאמר התם כלה תנן משמע התם שדרך לשתות בפני רבים בלא חזרת פניו היינו בשעת סעודה דומיא דכלה ובהלכות דרך ארץ אמרינן דברבים הופך פניו לצד אחר וישתה מים נראה דנקט מים לפי שאין רגילין לשתות כולן מים אלא הצמא בלבד אבל שאר דברים רגילין לשתות יחד ור"ת אומר דה"ק דאפילו לאותן הצנועים שלא לשתות מים בפני רבים לא ליהוי צנוע להטיל מים שמא ימתין ויסתכן:
notes.en: And they may not drink water in public: Rashi explained that it is the way of Torah scholars to be modest in eating and drinking. As for what is said at the end of Keitzad Tzolin (Pesaḥim 86b), that Rav Huna son of Rav Natan drank a cup in two draughts without turning his face away, and he said there, “We learned [this rule only of] a bride,” which implies that it is customary to drink in public without turning one’s face: that is at a meal, like a bride. And in Hilkhot Derekh Eretz we say that in public he should turn his face to another side and drink. It seems that it mentions water because not everyone usually drinks water, only one who is thirsty, whereas other drinks people usually drink together. Rabbeinu Tam says it means this: even for those modest people who do not drink water in public, one should not be modest about urinating, lest he wait and endanger himself.

notes.he: דסכנה היא להעמיד עצמו ואין שותין מים בפני רבים דלא דרך ארץ הוא:
notes.en: They urinate in public: for it is dangerous to hold oneself back. And they do not drink water in public: for that is not proper manners [derekh eretz].

messages.text: Torah scholars may urinate in public, but they may not drink water in public. And there was an incident involving one who sought to urinate, and he did not urinate, and his belly was found to be swollen.
messages.lead: And this is also taught in a baraita:

notes.he: ונמצא כרסו צבה נפוח:
notes.en: And his belly was found tzava: swollen.

messages.text: It was necessary for Shmuel to urinate on the Shabbat when everyone came to hear halakhot relating to the impending Festival. In order to afford him privacy, they spread a sheet for him. Shmuel then came before his father, who said to him:

notes.he: להטיל מים:
notes.en: It was necessary for him: to urinate.

notes.he: שלשים יום קודם הרגל דשואלין ודורשין בהלכות הרגל כדאמרינן במגילה (דף ד.):
notes.en: On the Shabbat of the Festival: [in the] thirty days before the Festival, when people ask and expound the halakhot of the Festival, as we say in Megilla (4a).

notes.he: פרסו סדין בינו לבין העם:
notes.en: They spread a cloak for him: they spread a sheet between him and the people.

notes.he: לקטנים:
notes.en: It was necessary for him: [to pass] urine.

notes.he: להפסיק בינו לבין העם משום צניעותא:
notes.en: They spread a cloak for him: to separate him from the people, for the sake of modesty.

notes.he: אתא א"ל לאבוהא היאך נגד גלימא:
notes.en: He came [and] told his father how they had spread a cloak.

messages.text: @Shmuel I will give you four hundred dinars if you will go and retract this incident, i.e., if you will state publicly that one may not hold back from urinating even at the expense of one’s privacy.

notes.he: דרוש שאסור להמתין מלהטיל מים עד שיהא לו צניעות:
notes.en: Retract the incident: expound that it is forbidden to hold back from urinating until one has privacy.

notes.dh: א"ל אתן לך ת' זוזי וזיל אהדר עובדא למריה
notes.he: כלומר שתעמיד הדבר על הילכתו. שתשתין לפניהם בגלוי כדי שלא ילמדו ממך שלא יסתכנו להעמיד על עצמם:
notes.en: He said to him: I will give you four hundred zuz, and go and set the incident right. That is, establish the matter according to its halakha: urinate before them openly, so that they will not learn from you to endanger themselves by holding back.

messages.text: Since you are an important man, you can have others spread a sheet around you. But with regard to one who cannot have others spread a sheet for him, should he endanger himself by seeking privacy? You must therefore teach that one should not hold back from urinating even in public.

notes.he: לפרוש סדין לפי שחשוב אתה:
notes.en: You, who can: have a sheet spread, because you are important.

notes.he: ואי ליצטרך אינש אחרינא דלא אפשר ליה וימתין עד שילכו העם ויסתכן ויהא עקור:
notes.en: But if another person needed to and could not, he would wait until the people left, and endanger himself, and become barren.

notes.he: דאית לך גלימא אפשר לך למפשט ודלא אפשר ליה דלית ליה גלימא למפשט יעמיד עצמו ומסתכן:
notes.en: You: who have a cloak, can spread it. But one who cannot, since he has no cloak to spread, will hold himself back and be endangered.

messages.text: It was necessary for Mar bar Rav Ashi to urinate while he was walking on the beams of a bridge, and therefore he urinated. They said to him: Your mother-in-law is coming.

notes.he: חמותך:
notes.en: Ḥamatakh: your mother-in-law.

messages.text: I would have done this even in her ear.

notes.he: אפילו בתוך אזנה הייתי מטיל מים אם לא היה לי מקום אחר קודם שאמתין וכ"ש בפניה:
notes.en: In her ear: even into her ear I would urinate, if I had no other place, rather than wait; all the more so in front of her.

notes.he: כלומר אפילו באודנא הוינא משתין מקמי דאיסתכן:
notes.en: In her ear: that is, I would urinate even in her ear before I would endanger myself.

messages.text: Since holding back from urinating would place him in physical danger, he would not care that his mother-in-law was coming and might see him.
And let me derive, i.e., can it not be said, that his belly swelled due to a leech that entered his intestines?
messages.quote: and his belly was found to be swollen

notes.he: דקתני לעיל שבקש להשתין ולא השתין ונמצא כריסו צבה ממאי דמשום המתנה הוה ליה דלמא עלקא שתה שקורין שנשוא"ה לפיכך צבה כריסו:
notes.en: And let me derive it from a leech: it was taught above that he sought to urinate and did not, and his belly was found swollen. From where [do we know] that this came from the waiting? Perhaps he swallowed a leech (Rashi adds an Old French gloss), and that is why his belly swelled.

notes.he: כלומר דהאי דכרסו צבה לאו מחמת שתן הוא אלא משום דשתה עלקה:
notes.en: And let me derive it from a leech: that is, that his belly was swollen not because of urine but because he swallowed a leech.

messages.text: The baraita is referring to a case where his urine would thereafter drip and no longer flowed in a healthy manner. Evidently, his health problems resulted from damage to the urinary tract.

notes.he: שאינו יכול להטיל מים יפה לאחר כן אלא שותת טיפין טיפין דודאי מחמת עיכוב שתן הוה ליה:
notes.en: Where it drips: he cannot urinate properly afterward, only drop by drop; that certainly came from holding back the urine.

notes.he: מים דאי שתה עלקה לא הוה שותת:
notes.en: Where it drips: the urine; for had he swallowed a leech, it would not drip.

messages.text: There are two orifices in a man. One of them expels urine and one of them expels semen, and there is only a partition about the thickness of a garlic peel between them. When a man needs to urinate and withholds the urine, if his urinary duct and seminal duct were punctured such that this duct leads into that one, he will be found to be barren, as his urine will penetrate into his seminal duct.
messages.lead: Concerning this topic the Sages taught in a baraita:

notes.he: ומעמיד עצמו ניקבו:
notes.en: At the time when a person needs: and holds himself back, they are punctured.

messages.text: What is the meaning of that which is written: “There shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle”? It means as follows: When will there not be a barren male among you? At a time that you act as among your cattle, i.e., you urinate when the need arises, without hesitation.

verse.he: בָּרוּךְ תִּהְיֶה מִכׇּל־הָעַמִּים לֹא־יִהְיֶה בְךָ עָקָר וַעֲקָרָה וּבִבְהֶמְתֶּךָ׃
verse.en: You shall be blessed above all other peoples: there shall be no sterile male or female among you or among your livestock.

notes.he: שתשים עצמך כבהמה שלא תהא צנוע בהטלת מים:
notes.en: At a time that you are as among your cattle: when you make yourself like an animal, not being modest about urinating.

notes.dh: אימתי לא יהיה בך עקר ועקרה בזמן שבבהמתך
notes.he: תימה היאך יכולין להשים עצמן כבהמה בהטלת מים שהיו צריכין לצאת חוץ מן המחנה ולהרחיק ג' פרסאות כדאמרי' בפ' בתרא דיומא (דף עה:) דאין נפנים לא בצדיהם ולא לפניהם אלא לאחריהם והיינו אפילו בקטנים דבפרק מי שמתו (ברכות דף כה.) מוקמא ויתד תהיה לך מחוץ למחנה ויצאת וגו' בקטנים:
notes.en: When will there not be a barren male or female among you? At a time that [you are] as among your cattle: This is puzzling: how could they make themselves like an animal in urinating, when they had to go outside the camp and go three parasangs away, as we say in the last chapter of Yoma (75b), and they relieved themselves neither to their sides nor in front of them, only behind them? And this applies even to urinating, for in chapter Mi Shemetu (Berakhot 25a) the verse “And you shall have a place outside the camp, and you shall go out there” is explained as referring to urine.

notes.he: בזמן שבבהמתך כשאתה משים עצמך כבהמה שמשתנת בפני רבים לא יהיה בך עקר ועקרה:
notes.en: At a time that [you are] as among your cattle: when you make yourself like an animal, which urinates in front of many, there will be no barren male or female among you.

messages.text: The phrase “There shall not be male…barren among you” means you will not be barren of students, as one who leaves behind no students is considered barren. The term “or female barren” indicates that your prayers will not be barren, i.e., unheard, before the Omnipresent, but will be heard by Him. And when will they be heard? At a time when you place yourself in prayer as an animal, with humility.
messages.lead: With regard to the same verse:

notes.he: וכשתתפלל [על בנים] תהא נשמעת תפלתך:
notes.en: That your prayer will not be barren, etc.: when you pray [for children], your prayer will be heard.

notes.he: שלא תמתין מלהטיל מים:
notes.en: As an animal: that you do not hold back from urinating.

notes.dh: שלא תהא תפלתך עקורה לפני המקום בזמן שאתה משים עצמך כבהמה
notes.he: פירש בקונטרס שלא תהא עקורה כשאתה מתפלל על בנים ונראה דלכל תפלה קאמר כדאמר שאין העולם מתקיים אלא במי שמשים עצמו כבהמה כדכתיב אדם ובהמה תושיע ה' ובמי שמשים עצמו כמי שאינו כדכתיב (איוב כ״ו:ז׳) תולה ארץ על בלימה (חולין דף פט.):
notes.en: That your prayer will not be barren before the Omnipresent, at a time when you make yourself as an animal: Rashi explained that it will not be barren when you pray for children. But it seems that it speaks of every prayer, as it says that the world endures only for the sake of one who makes himself like an animal, as it is written: “Man and beast You preserve, O Lord,” and for the sake of one who makes himself as if he is nothing, as it is written: “He hangs the earth upon nothing [belima]” (Job 26:7) (Ḥullin 89a).

notes.he: אין תפלתך עקורה כשאתה מתפלל על עסקי בנים בזמן שאתה משים עצמך כבהמה שלא העמדת עצמך:
notes.en: When: is your prayer not barren, when you pray about children? At a time when you make yourself like an animal, not holding yourself back.

messages.text: A person should urinate in Babylonia only on the dust, as it absorbs the urine. He should not urinate either on an earthenware vessel or on a hard place, as the urine will not be absorbed and will eventually flow into the underwater rivers.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites additional statements of the Sages with regard to urination.

notes.he: בתוך עביט של מימי רגלים לפי שמשליכין אותו בנהר בסמוך להם ונהרות בבל הולכין ומתעכבין בעין עיטם כדמפרש:
notes.en: Not on an earthenware vessel: into a chamber pot, because they throw it into a nearby river, and the rivers of Babylonia flow on and collect at Ein Eitam, as is explained.

notes.he: שאינן בולעין וצפין על הקרקע עד שנשטפין למקום מדרון ונופלין לנהר:
notes.en: Nor on a hard place: which does not absorb; [the urine] floats on the ground until it is washed down a slope and falls into the river.

notes.dh: לא ישתין אדם מים לא על (גבי) [כלי] חרס ולא על גבי מקום קשה
notes.he: הנך חומרות דוקא בבבל כדאמר טעמא משום דהני מודרי דבבל מהדרי מיא לעיטם שעל נהר פרת דדרך המים ללכת דרך הילוכם לעין עיטם דפרת מתערב בכל מימות שבעולם כדאמר לקמן בפ"ט (בכורות דף נה.) הנודר ממימי פרת אסור בכל מימות שבעולם ואפילו עינאתא דמדלייא אמרינן לקמן דהנהו סולמי דפרת נינהו ובסוכה (דף נג.) נמי אמרינן דכרינן פורתא ונבעי מיא הנהו סולמי דפרת הוו ואע"ג דסולמי דפרת מתערבין בכל מימות שבעולם אין לאסור אלא שבבבל כדפרישית שדרך הילוכו של פרת מתערב בעין עיטם והוה משמע מכאן דפרת הולך מבבל לא"י אבל שאלתי לאחד מא"י ואמר לי שיורד מא"י לבבל וכן מוכח לקמן בפ"ט (בכורות דף נה:) דאמרינן מטרא במערבא סהדא רבא פרת וכן פירש שם בקונט' וזהו דוחק לומר דאפילו הולך מבבל לא"י ניכר כשגדל הנהר מחמת רוב גשמים ומתרבה הנהר לאחוריו מתוך רבוי המים:
notes.en: A person should not urinate on an earthenware vessel or on a hard place: These stringencies apply only in Babylonia, since the reason given is that those inclines of Babylonia return the water to Eitam, on the Euphrates, for the water flows along its course to Ein Eitam, because the Euphrates mixes with all the waters in the world, as it says below in chapter 9 (Bekhorot 55a): one who vows not to benefit from the waters of the Euphrates is forbidden all the waters in the world. And even springs that rise up, we say below, are offshoots of the Euphrates; and in Sukka (53a) too we say, “Let us dig a little and seek water”: those are offshoots of the Euphrates. Even though the offshoots of the Euphrates mix with all the waters in the world, it is forbidden only in Babylonia, as I explained, since the Euphrates’ course mixes into Ein Eitam. From here it would seem that the Euphrates flows from Babylonia to the Land of Israel. But I asked someone from the Land of Israel, and he told me that it flows down from the Land of Israel to Babylonia. So it is also evident below in chapter 9 (Bekhorot 55b), where we say: “Of rain in the West [the Land of Israel], the Euphrates is the great witness,” and so Rashi explained there. And it is strained to say that even though it flows from Babylonia to the Land of Israel, [the rain] shows when the river rises from heavy rains and swells backward from the abundance of water.

messages.text: Those inclines of Babylonia return the water through underground watercourses to the Spring of Eitam in Eretz Yisrael, from which water was taken to the Temple.

notes.he: מקומות מדרון שבבבל:
notes.en: And Rav says, those inclines of Babylonia: the sloping places in Babylonia.

notes.he: שבו כ"ג טובל ביוה"כ כדאמרי' במסכת יומא בפרק ג' (דף לא.):
notes.en: Return [the water] to Ein Eitam: where the High Priest immersed on Yom Kippur, as we say in tractate Yoma, chapter three (31a).

notes.he: מדרונות של בבל אם משתין עליהם מהדרי המי רגלים לעין עיטם לנהר שמושך לארץ ישראל ויהיו שותין ממנו לפיכך לא ישתין אלא על מקום נמוך שיבלעו שם העין:
notes.en: Those inclines of Babylonia: the slopes of Babylonia. If one urinates on them, the urine flows back to Ein Eitam, to the river that runs toward the Land of Israel, and people would drink from it. Therefore he should urinate only on a low place, so that it is absorbed there [and does not reach] the spring.

messages.text: A woman should not stand openly in front of a child when she urinates. But if she urinates while turning sideways, we have no problem with it.

notes.he: כשהיא מטלת אל תעמוד ממש כנגד התינוקות דחוצפתא היא:
notes.en: Should not stand openly in front of a child: when she urinates, she should not stand directly facing the children, for that is brazen.

notes.he: אם לצד אחר שאין משתנת בפני התינוק ל"ל בה:
notes.en: Sideways: if [she turns] to the other side, so that she does not urinate facing the child, we have no problem with it.

notes.dh: האי איתתא לא תיקום להדיא באפי ינוקא
notes.he: אע"ג שאינה מגלה עצמה איכא חוצפא כשהיא מטילה מים והתינוק עומד בפניה דהא אין דרך אשה לגלות עצמה לפניה לא לקטנים ולא לגדולים כדמוכח בפ' מי שמתו (ברכות דף כג:):
notes.en: This woman should not stand openly in front of a child: even though she does not expose herself, it is brazen when she urinates with the child standing in front of her, for it is not the way of a woman to expose herself before anyone, neither children nor adults, as is evident in chapter Mi Shemetu (Berakhot 23b).

notes.he: כשמשתין משום צניעותא. אגיסא דמהדרא אפה לית לן בה:
notes.en: Should not stand openly in front of a child: when she urinates, for the sake of modesty. Sideways, when she turns her face away, we have no problem with it.

messages.text: A mass of feces that is held back without being discharged causes a person to suffer from dropsy [hidrokan], while a stream of urine that is held back causes a person to suffer from jaundice.

notes.he: גדולים:
notes.en: A mass [amud]: of feces.

notes.he: חולי מעיים:
notes.en: Hidrokan: an illness of the intestines.

notes.he: קטנים:
notes.en: A stream [silon]: of urine.

notes.he: משמע דהדרוקן וירקון תרי מילי נינהו ומיהו נראה שהם ענין אחד דאמרי' ביבמות (דף ס:) העבירום לפני ציץ כל שראויה לביאה פניה מוריקות דאמר סימן לעבירה הדרוקן:
notes.en: Brings him to dropsy [hidrokan] … brings him to jaundice [yerakon]: this implies that hidrokan and yerakon are two different things. Yet it seems they are one matter, for we say in Yevamot (60b): they passed them before the [High Priest’s] frontplate, and any girl fit for intercourse, her face turned yellow [morikot]; and it says, a sign of transgression is hidrokan.

notes.he: היינו כריסו צבה:
notes.en: Hidrokan: that is, his belly is swollen.

notes.he: חולי ירקון:
notes.en: Yerakon: the illness of jaundice.

messages.text: If one’s blood levels increase due to not undergoing bloodletting often enough, then boils will increase on him as well. If one’s semen levels increase due to not engaging in sexual intercourse often enough, then leprosy will increase on him. If one’s feces levels increase due to not relieving himself enough, dropsy will increase in him. Finally, if one’s urine levels increase due to not relieving himself enough, then jaundice will increase as well.

notes.he: המרבה דם שאינו מקיז מרבה שחין:
notes.en: Much blood, many boils: one who has much blood and does not let blood gets many boils.

notes.he: מי שיש לו אשה ואינו משמש מטתו מרבה צרעת:
notes.en: Much semen: one who has a wife and does not have relations with her gets much leprosy.

notes.he: שמעמיד שאינו מקיז דם:
notes.en: Much blood: when he holds back and does not let blood.

notes.he: כלומר לוקה בשחין:
notes.en: Many boils: that is, he is stricken with boils.

messages.text: What is this melancholy temper?
messages.quote: who is afflicted with a melancholy temper

messages.text: A fallen spirit, i.e., the spirit of a demon, has come upon him.

notes.he: נאלת רוח שטות ע"י שד זהו בן נפילים נוייטו"ן:
notes.en: A spirit of folly has seized [him], through a demon; this is ben nefilim (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: דתנן דהוי מום מאי ניהו נאלא רוח שטות:
notes.en: A ruaḥ ketzarot comes upon him: which the mishna taught is a blemish. What is it? A spirit of folly has seized [him].

notes.he: רוח שידה שגעון:
notes.en: Ben nefalim: a demon’s spirit; madness.

messages.text: The mishna also teaches that one whose scrotum is unnaturally long [me’ushban] and one whose penis is unnaturally long [ba’al gever] are disqualified from performing the Temple service.
A meshuban is one with exceedingly large testicles, and a ba’al gever is one with an unnaturally long penis.

notes.he: משוכן בביצים שביציו גדולים ביותר:
notes.en: The meshukhan and the ba’al garav [so Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads, for meshuban and ba’al gever]: meshukhan in the testicles, whose testicles are exceedingly large.

notes.he: בעל גרב [גבר] בגיד שארוך ביותר:
notes.en: Ba’al garav [read: gever]: in the member, which is exceedingly long.

messages.text: A meshuban, this is synonymous with the kayyan. The garbetan, this is synonymous with a ba’al kik. A kayyan is one with a condition of the testicles, while a garbeta is one with a condition of the penis.

notes.he: היינו משובן:
notes.en: The kayyan: that is the meshuban.

notes.he: היינו מין בעל גבר:
notes.en: The garbetan: that is a kind of ba’al gever.

notes.he: שביציו גדולים:
notes.en: In the testicles: his testicles are large.

notes.he: שגידו גדול:
notes.en: In the member: his member is large.

messages.text: And how much is considered too long, which disqualifies the priest from performing the Temple service?

notes.he: יגדל הגיד שיהא פסול:
notes.en: And how much: must the member grow for him to be disqualified?

messages.text: Until the knee.

notes.he: רב יהודה שארוך הגיד עד הארכובה:
notes.en: He pointed: Rav Yehuda [indicated] that the member is long down to the knee.

messages.text: If one’s penis reaches until his knee he is disqualified from performing the Temple service. But if it reaches until just above his knee he remains fit.
If his penis reaches until the knee he is fit, but if it passes below the knee he is disqualified.
Mishna
If one has no testicles, or if he has only one testicle, that is the mero’aḥ ashekh that is stated in the Torah among the blemishes that disqualify a priest from Temple service.

verse.he: אוֹ־גִבֵּן אוֹ־דַק אוֹ תְּבַלֻּל בְּעֵינוֹ אוֹ גָרָב אוֹ יַלֶּפֶת אוֹ מְרוֹחַ אָשֶׁךְ׃
verse.en: or who is a hunchback, or a dwarf, or who has a growth in his eye, or who has a boil-scar, or scurvy, or crushed testes.

messages.text: A mero’aḥ ashekh is anyone whose testicles were crushed.

notes.he: שנימוחו ביציו:
notes.en: Whose testicles were crushed: his testicles were crushed [nimoḥu].

notes.he: נימוחו ביציו:
notes.en: Whose testicles were crushed: his testicles were crushed [nimoḥu].

messages.text: It is anyone that has wind in his testicles, i.e., they are swollen.

notes.he: שביציו נפוחים:
notes.en: That has wind in his testicles: his testicles are swollen.

notes.he: שנפוחין ביציו:
notes.en: That has wind in his testicles: his testicles are swollen.

messages.text: Mero’aḥ ashekh does not refer to the testicles; rather, the reference is to anyone whose appearance [marav] is especially dark [ḥashukhin].

notes.he: שהוא שחור ככושי. ולא בביצים משתעי כלל:
notes.en: Whose appearance is dark: he is black like a Kushite. And [the verse] does not speak of the testicles at all.

notes.he: שהוא שחור ככושי:
notes.en: Whose appearance is dark: he is black like a Kushite.

messages.text: Gemara

The Gemara explains why the tanna’im interpret mero’aḥ ashekh in different ways. It is difficult for Rabbi Yishmael: If mero’aḥ ashekh is referring to one who lacks two testicles, then the Torah should have stated: Ḥasar ashekh, lacking a testicle, rather than mero’aḥ ashekh. Therefore, he teaches that it is referring to one whose testicles were crushed.

notes.he: כלומר להכי פליג רבי ישמעאל את"ק משום דקשיא ליה א"כ דבשאין לו ביצים מישתעי קרא חסר אשך מיבעי ליה:
notes.en: It is difficult for Rabbi Yishmael: that is, this is why Rabbi Yishmael disagrees with the first tanna: it is difficult for him that if the verse speaks of one who has no testicles, it should have said ḥasar ashekh.

notes.he: להכי תני ר"י שנמרחו אשכיו:
notes.en: He teaches, whose testicles were crushed: this is why Rabbi Yishmael teaches “whose testicles were crushed.”

notes.he: אם כדברי ת"ק חסר אשך מיבעי ליה אלא תני שנמרחו. וכן קשיא ליה לרבי עקיבא מאי דאמר ר' ישמעאל וכל חד וחד בעי לתרוצי טעמיה:
notes.en: It is difficult for Rabbi Yishmael: if it were as the first tanna says, it should have said ḥasar ashekh; so he teaches, “whose testicles were crushed.” And likewise what Rabbi Yishmael said is difficult for Rabbi Akiva. Each one seeks to answer [with] his own reasoning.

messages.text: This is difficult for Rabbi Akiva: If mero’aḥ ashekh means one with crushed testicles, then the Torah should have stated: Mimro’aḥ ashekh, crushed testicles, not mero’aḥ ashekh. Therefore, he teaches that the Torah is referring to one who has wind in his testicles.

notes.he: דהא מ"ם דמרוח משמשת היא:
notes.en: It should have said mimro’aḥ ashekh: for the mem of mero’aḥ is a servile letter [a prefix, not part of the root].

messages.text: This is difficult for Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus: If mero’aḥ ashekh is referring to one with wind in his testicles, then the Torah should have stated: Ruaḥ ashekh, wind in the testicles. Therefore, he teaches that the Torah is speaking of anyone whose appearance is especially dark.
messages.quote: anyone whose appearance [marav] is especially dark [ḥashukhin]

messages.text: And how does he derive such an interpretation from the verse? He holds that the Sages subtract and add and interpret homiletically. Accordingly, the ḥet of mero’aḥ is removed along with the alef of ashekh. The ḥet is added to ashekh and the alef is added to mero’aḥ, and mero’aḥ ashekh is rearranged to state: Marav ḥashukhin, his appearance is dark.

notes.he: גורעין חי"ת ממרוח ואלף מאשך ומוסיפין ח' במקום אלף על אשך ואלף במקום חי"ת על מרוח והוי מרואו חשך:
notes.en: Subtract and add: they subtract the ḥet from mero’aḥ and the alef from ashekh, and add a ḥet in place of the alef to ashekh and an alef in place of the ḥet to mero’aḥ, and it becomes mar’o ḥoshekh [his appearance is dark].

notes.he: ר' חנניה גורעין ומוספין ודורשין. גורעין [א'] מאשך. ומוסיפין אותו במרוח והוה ליה מראה וגורעין ח' ממרוח ומוסיפין במקום א' שבאשך והוה ליה חשך והיינו מראו חשך שמראיו חשוכין:
notes.en: He holds: Rabbi Ḥanina holds that one subtracts, adds and expounds. One subtracts the [alef] from ashekh and adds it in mero’aḥ, which becomes mar’eh [appearance]; and one subtracts the ḥet from mero’aḥ and adds it in place of the alef in ashekh, which becomes ḥoshekh [dark]. That is mar’o ḥoshekh: whose appearance is dark.

messages.caption: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus’s reading: swap two letters and mero’aḥ ashekh becomes mar’av ḥashukh, “his appearance is dark.”

messages.text: But if so, this is identical to one whose skin is extremely black, and the mishna on 45b explicitly states that such a priest is disqualified from performing the Temple service.

notes.he: וכושי בהדיא קתני מתני (לקמן בכורות מה.) הכושי והגיחור:
notes.en: This is the Kushite: and the mishna below (45a) [printed on our daf on 45b] teaches the Kushite explicitly: “the kushi and the giḥor.”

messages.text: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus learns from the mishna only that a mero’aḥ ashekh is disqualified; he does not teach in that mishna the halakha that a person with extremely black skin is blemished.
Mishna

The mishna lists additional blemishes that disqualify a priest from performing the Temple service: One whose legs are crooked and bend inward, causing him to knock his ankles or his knees into each other as he walks,

notes.he: שארכבותיו עוקמות לחוץ וקרסוליו לפנים ונוקשין זה לזה כשהוא מהלך. ובארכבותיו היינו איפכא שרגליו עקומות לחוץ ומרחיק זה מזה עד שארכבותיו מלמעלה העקומות כלפי פנים נוקשות זו לזו:
notes.en: One who knocks his ankles: his knees are bent outward and his ankles inward, and they knock against each other as he walks. And “his knees” is the reverse: his legs are bent outward and he keeps them apart, until his knees, which bend inward above, knock against each other.

notes.he: שכשהוא הולך קרסוליו או ארכבותיו נוקשות זו בזו והיינו הקישן דאמרינן בגמרא:
notes.en: One who knocks his ankles and his knees: when he walks, his ankles or his knees knock against each other; and that is the hakishan we speak of in the Gemara.

messages.text: The mishna’s list continues on 45a.
